what_this_pins: A mirror that produces geometry coinciding with the original WELDS THE VERTICES AND LEAVES THE FACES DOUBLED. The reference editor behaves this way. A mesh with 8 vertices, 12 edges and 12 faces, every edge incident to four faces, is the correct output of mirroring a cube across its own symmetry plane with vertex-merge on -- it is not a defect.

Collapsing coincident faces is a SEPARATE, EXPLICITLY INVOKED operation. It is not part of the mirror, not part of any other duplication (array/clone/radial/rail), and not part of the vertex weld: welding two coincident cubes down to 8 shared vertices still leaves 12 faces.

The collapse IGNORES WINDING. Two faces on the same vertex ring collapse whether the rings run the same way or opposite ways. The reference's own documentation says 'and face the same direction'; that is measurably false.

The collapse test is exact VERTEX IDENTITY, not position: two meshes at identical coordinates with their own vertex records do not collapse at all. The collapse therefore has NO tolerance of its own -- the only tolerance in the pipeline is the vertex weld's, and it reaches faces only through vertex identity.

The collapse test is the cyclic RING (up to rotation and reversal), NOT the vertex SET. Two faces on the same four vertices in an order that is neither a rotation nor a reversal of each other are left alone.
The survivor is the earlier polygon, kept byte-identical: same ring, same winding, same tags. Nothing is flipped and nothing is merged into it.
A face lying IN the mirror plane yields a duplicated face with ZERO non-manifold edges. A duplicate-face defect taxonomy keyed on edge valence cannot see this case.

cube.description: unit cube centred on the origin, spanning [-0.5, +0.5] on every axis; faces wound outward

cube_shifted.description: the same cube translated so it spans x in [0, 1]; the x = 0 face lies IN the mirror plane

plane_quad.description: a single quad lying IN the mirror plane z = 0

doubled_cube.description: the cube's 8 vertices carrying 12 faces: the 6 originals plus 6 duplicates on the SAME vertex records. This is what a self-coincident mirror leaves behind.
doubled_cube.faces_from: cube + a second copy (see each case for the ring order used)

two_independent_cubes.description: two complete cubes at IDENTICAL coordinates, each with its own 8 vertex records: 16 vertices, 12 faces, no shared vertex
two_independent_cubes.faces: cube faces, plus the same rings with every index offset by 8

mirror_cases.name: self_coincident_merge_on
mirror_cases.op: mirror across the plane x = 0, vertex-merge ON
mirror_cases.new_face_note: each new ring is a cyclic ROTATION of an original ring with the SAME winding: the mirror's own polygon flip cancels the reflection's reversal on a closed solid. This case therefore CANNOT discriminate a winding-sensitive collapse from a winding-blind one -- the doubled_cube cases below are what discriminate it.

mirror_cases.name: self_coincident_merge_off
mirror_cases.op: mirror across the plane x = 0, vertex-merge OFF

mirror_cases.name: self_coincident_then_explicit_collapse
mirror_cases.op: mirror across x = 0 with merge ON, then the explicit duplicate-polygon collapse over the whole mesh
mirror_cases.surviving_face_note: the six ORIGINAL rings, verbatim -- identical order, identical winding. The later (mirrored) polygon is the one deleted.

mirror_cases.name: seam_plane_touches_geometry
mirror_cases.op: mirror across the plane x = 0, vertex-merge ON
mirror_cases.note: the four seam vertices weld; the seam face is left DOUBLED, and its two copies have OPPOSITE winding ([0,4,7,3] and [0,3,7,4]). The four seam edges are the only non-manifold ones.

mirror_cases.name: face_lying_in_the_mirror_plane
mirror_cases.op: mirror across the plane z = 0, vertex-merge ON
mirror_cases.note: a duplicated face with ZERO non-manifold edges -- the cell a valence-based duplicate detector is blind to. The pair here IS reversed, so this case discriminates winding, and the collapse still removes one.

mirror_cases.name: plane_cuts_through_at_no_symmetry
mirror_cases.op: mirror across the plane x = 0.25, vertex-merge ON
mirror_cases.note: the plane passes through the solid but nothing coincides, so nothing welds and nothing doubles. Control for the two cases above.

mirror_cases.name: no_selection
mirror_cases.op: mirror across x = 0 with merge ON and NO face selection
mirror_cases.note: empty selection means the whole mesh, identical to selecting every face.

collapse_law_cases.name: reversed_duplicates
collapse_law_cases.pins: winding is IGNORED -- this is the case the reference's own help text says should not collapse

collapse_law_cases.name: same_winding_duplicates
collapse_law_cases.pins: control for the row above: both windings collapse, so the rule is winding-blind, not winding-inverted

collapse_law_cases.name: rotated_ring_duplicates
collapse_law_cases.duplicate_rings: each original ring cyclically rotated by one
collapse_law_cases.pins: the ring's start index does not matter

collapse_law_cases.name: same_vertex_set_different_ring
collapse_law_cases.rig: one quad on 4 vertices, rings [0,1,2,3] and [0,2,1,3]
collapse_law_cases.pins: the test is the cyclic RING up to rotation and reversal, NOT the vertex SET. A collapse keyed on a sorted vertex set would wrongly merge these two, which are different polygons (one convex, one self-crossing).

collapse_law_cases.name: coincident_but_unwelded
collapse_law_cases.pins: no positional term at all: identical coordinates are not enough, the faces must reference the SAME vertex records

collapse_law_cases.name: weld_then_collapse
collapse_law_cases.pins: the vertex weld alone does NOT remove the doubled faces. Ownership: weld and face-collapse are two independent passes, and only the weld is ever run implicitly.

collapse_law_cases.name: partial_overlap
collapse_law_cases.pins: a shared majority of vertices is not a collapse

collapse_law_cases.name: different_material_tags
collapse_law_cases.duplicate_rings: reversed, and tagged with a different material
collapse_law_cases.surviving_material: the material of the EARLIER polygon
collapse_law_cases.pins: by default the collapse refuses when the two faces carry different material or part tags; a force flag bypasses both tag gates. The survivor keeps its own tag -- tags are not merged.

collapse_law_cases.name: only_one_of_the_pair_selected
collapse_law_cases.pins: the selection chooses which faces are EXAMINED; the partner that gets deleted need not be selected. Exactly one face was removed.

collapse_law_cases.name: no_selection
collapse_law_cases.pins: an empty selection means the whole mesh

weld_tolerance.shape: Chebyshev (per-axis, axis-aligned box), NOT a Euclidean radius; the per-axis differences are taken in 32-bit floating point and compared against a double tolerance.

automatic_mode.law: tolerance = maxAbsCoordinate(bounding box of the SOURCE vertices) / 336000
automatic_mode.note: the term is the largest ABSOLUTE COORDINATE of the box, not its extent -- see the discriminator below. Two vertices weld iff every axis difference is <= that tolerance.
automatic_mode.extent_vs_max_abs_discriminator: a unit cube translated to x = 1000 has the SAME extent (1.0) and 2001x the max absolute coordinate. Its threshold moved by ~2000x, so the tolerance follows the max absolute coordinate. An extent-based rule predicts no change at all and is refuted.

fixed_mode.law: tolerance = the distance the caller supplies, exactly

provenance.harness: headless scripted capture, one process, private isolated profile; scripts and raw per-case results live in the private tree
provenance.notes: The capture had TWO arms and both are load-bearing: a static read of the shipped binary enumerated the candidate mechanisms (which layer owns a collapse at all, and that the equivalence predicate returns +1/-1 while its caller tests only != 0), and four headless boots selected among them and produced these numbers. `source` records the arm the NUMBERS came from -- the enum has no 'static-read' value, and inventing one made provenance_check.py reject the whole file, which is worse than recording the static arm here in prose. The ownership and winding answers were read out of the shipped binary first (the duplicate-polygon predicate and its complete caller set) and then confirmed by 19 + 24 + 20 live cells. The reference's own help text disagrees with both the binary and the measurement on the winding question; the measurement is what this fixture records.

_classification_note: Everything ABOVE this line is the capture, promoted byte-identical from the private toolcard. Everything BELOW is vibe3d's own reading of it, added when the fixture was promoted (task 1560) and maintained on our side.

classification.verdict: the mirror agrees in full; the explicit collapse agrees on every row our kernel can express except its coincidence KEY

vibe3d_measured.comment: The AGREEMENT rows, measured 2026-08-20 on Mesh.mirrorFacesPlane / Mesh.unifyFaces at the tip of task/mirror-nonmanifold. Kept short on purpose: the numbers themselves live in mirror_cases / collapse_law_cases above and the test reads them from there, so a second copy here could only drift. What is recorded is WHICH rows were driven and that they agreed.

not_covered_here.comment: Rows the capture pins that our kernel has no way to answer. Recorded rather than quietly dropped -- a fixture row nobody reads is decoration, and a row nobody CAN read should say why.
not_covered_here.different_material_tags: our duplicate-face pass has no material or part gate at all: it neither refuses on differing tags nor offers a force flag, so neither the default nor the forced branch of this row is expressible. A capability gap, not a divergence in a shared behaviour.
not_covered_here.only_one_of_the_pair_selected: our pass takes no selection and always scans the whole mesh, so 'the selection chooses which faces are EXAMINED' has nothing to bind to.

divergences.comment: ONE entry per divergence, each with its own status, so retiring one cannot silence another. See doc/behavior_gap_registry.md for the process.

collapse_key_is_the_vertex_set.what: The captured law keys the collapse on the cyclic RING, up to rotation and reversal, on exact vertex indices. Mesh.unifyFaces keys it on the SORTED VERTEX SET (mesh_ops/cleanup.d, computeDuplicateFaceMask), so it merges two polygons that carry the same four vertices in an order that is neither a rotation nor a reversal of each other -- one convex quad and one self-crossing one, which the reference leaves alone. Every other collapse row agrees, so this is the key and nothing else.
collapse_key_is_the_vertex_set.reach: the collapse only, NOT the mirror. The mirror path never collapses faces at all, so no mirror cell is affected by this and none of the seven mirror rows moves when it is fixed.
collapse_key_is_the_vertex_set.closing_it: re-key computeDuplicateFaceMask on canonicalRing (min over rotations of the ring and of its reversal) instead of the sorted set, then flip status to "closed" and set vibe3d_faces_after to 2. The test asserts the gap-closed condition FIRST, so a landed fix fails saying exactly that.
